name: בית הלל vs. בית שמאי
about: Going up or going down each night.
focus: The two opinions, why we follow בית הלל, and the two ways of thinking behind them.
today: What’s one good thing you can add a little more of each day?
overview: The sages Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argued about how to light: start with eight candles and count down, or start with one and add one every night. We follow Beis Hillel - we always add more light.
reading: The גמרא (שבת כא) relates the מחלוקת (difference of opinion) between בית שמאי and בית הלל, about how we should light the מנורה.

head: בית שמאי says:
בית הלל says:
rows:
on the first night, we should light 8 candles,
on the second night 7,
on the third 6 - and so on – one candle less each night.

on the first night we light 1,
on the second night 2,
on the third night 3 - and so on – adding a candle each night.

reading: The גמרא brings 2 opinions about their reasoning:

head: בית שמאי
בית הלל
rows: Opinion #1
בית שמאי says to light as many candles – as the number of days still left to חנוכה. On the 1st day, light 8, because there are 8 days left. On the 2nd day, light 7, as there are seven days left.
בית הלל says to light the number of candles as the days that have already passed. On day 2, light 2, because it is the second day, etc.
Opinion #2
בית שמאי says we light less each night just like the קרבנות on סוכות, as they offer one Korbon less each night.
בית הלל says we must always increase in matters of holiness, not lessen.

reading: חנוכה is also an acronym for the words “ח' נרות והלכה כבית הלל” which means that we follow the הלכה of בית הלל in the way we light the מנורה.

בית הלל holds that we should add one light to the מנורה each night. Beis שמאי's opinion is that we start with 8 lights on the first night of חנוכה, 7 lights on the 2nd night, and work our way down to one light on the final night of חנוכה.

reading.p: The first night we light one candle. We add an additional light each night (the 2nd night, two candles, the third night, three and so on) until the eighth night, on which we light eight.

reading: On the first night, light the candle on the far right. On the second night, add a candle to its left and so on.

reading.p: Always light the newest candle first – the one on the left, and make your way towards the one on the right.

reading: “מצות נר חנוכה נר איש וביתו והמהדרין נר לכל אחד ואחד והמהדרין מן המהדרין בית שמאי אומרים יום ראשון מדליק שמנה מכאן ואילך פוחת והולך בית הלל אומרים יום ראשון מדליק אחת מכאן ואילך מוסיף והולך” — “The basic commandment of Chanukah lights is for the head of the household to light one candle for the entire family each night. Those who want to enhance their fulfillment of mitzvot light one candle each night for each member of the household. Those who desire to enhance their observance of mitzvot even further... According to Beit Shammai, the first day one kindles eight candles, and henceforth continuously decreases. According to Beit Hillel, the first day one lights one candle, and henceforth continuously increases.” (Shabbat 21b)

name: The number 8
focus: Why eight, and what eight stands for. (The Oil group covers the jar itself.)
today: When have you done something beyond what’s normal for you?
overview: Why is Chanukah eight days long, and not seven? The number eight is one step above the seven days of nature - it stands for miracles that are higher than nature.
reading: Why did the Miracle of the מנורה last for eight days – rather than any other number of days?
The most common answer is because it took eight days to prepare more olive oil for the מנורה.

reading.p: Why did it take 8 days to prepare the new oil?
list: It was a four day journey to the place where new pure oil could be made. To travel there and back with the new oil took eight days.
Since the Jewish People were טמא (impure) from the war, they waited seven days to become טהור (pure). On the eighth day they pressed new olive oil.

reading.h: Number eight is out of this world

reading: Earlier, we asked the famous question: Why did the נס of the מנורה last for eight days – rather than any other number of days?
The usual answer is that it took eight days to prepare more שמן זית for the מנורה.
There is also a deeper explanation.
The number eight is very special. Number seven symbolizes nature. Hashem created our world in seven days (six days and Shabbat), our week has seven days. Every object has seven areas of property:
1 top, 2 bottom, 3 right, 4 left, 5 front, 6 back, 7 center.
The usual way Hashem relates to this world is through Nature. The נסים of חנוכה however, were obvious, revealed miracles, both at war and with the מנורה.

reading.p: “The Nature” in Hebrew – הטבע 86 has the same גמטריא as א-להים. What people call “Nature” is really ה' in disguise. Now this level of ה' runs the world through “the program” we call “Nature”. There are higher levels to ה' – than just the Nature level. When ה' performs a נס – it is above Nature. When a צדיק Davens to ה' and causes a נס – the צדיק is reaching beyond the powers of Nature to change what should “naturally” happen. Through our תפילות and מעשים טובים we are able to rise above the laws of nature and cause nature to change – and miracles to happen – as it says, “אין מזל לישראל” meaning that we can rise above the “מזל” that rules nature.

reading: The number eight symbolizes “higher than nature”. Our ברית at 8 days old symbolizes that our connection with ה' is above Nature. The oil lasted in the מנורה for Eight days. The כהן גדול wears eight garments.

reading.p: The name of the חשמונאים hints to that special number eight. In Hebrew “חש – Chash” means “feels” and שמונה is eight. The Chash-Shmona'im “felt the eight” – they felt and were connected to a level that is higher than nature.

reading: In a different way, we see the number eight twice in their name:

While seven represents the natural order of the world (seven days of the week, cycle of seven years for Shemitah, etc.), the number eight represents the connection between G-d and the Jewish people that is higher than the natural order. It is for this reason that Chanukah, which represents this suprarational connection, was established for eight days. Likewise, we find in Midrashic sources that the era of the final redemption is represented by the number eight, which reflects a relationship with G-d that is higher than nature.

name: What were the יוונים after?
about: Their decrees and what they wanted.
focus: What the Greeks wanted, the three decrees, and the מתיונים.
today: What tries to pull Jews away from Torah today, and how do we stay strong?
overview: The Greeks did not only want to hurt the Jews - they wanted to uproot Torah and the Jewish way of life. When we know what the Yevanim were after, we understand what we are still standing up for today.
reading: More than 2000 years ago, the Syrian-Greeks ruled over ארץ ישראל. They were not happy with just ruling our bodies, they wanted to also ruin our souls. They wanted us to give up our holy way of life, to think and live as they did. Unfortunately, many Jews followed the Greek lifestyle and turned away from ה'.
ארץ ישראל was now under the rule of אנטיכוס – the Syrian-Greek king. As time went on, אנטיכוס continued oppressing the Jews, more than before.
When אנטיכוס III died, his son Seleucus IV took over – and continued to oppress the Jews, more than his father did with high taxes and evil laws.
By now, many Jews were being influenced by their Syrian-Greek neighbors to forget about ה' and His תורה and to adopt the Greek ways and lifestyle.

The Syrian-Greeks worshiped the human body. They put all their efforts into strengthening and beautifying the body. They held sport competitions and invented the Olympics. They left the spirit and soul matters far behind.
Truth, morals, values, purity and traditions – all the things that בני ישראל stand for - were not important to them, rather, it was all about physical beauty and pleasures of the body.

“Greece” in Hebrew Is יון. The “Greeks” are called יוונים. The Jews who tried to be like the Greeks were called מתיונים – the “יון Wanna Be”s, otherwise known as “Hellenists.” The Jews who remained faithful to ה' were named “חסידים.”

When אנטיכוס IV Epiphanies took over the kingdom, he did not tolerate the Jewish People living Jewishly. His soldiers roamed ארץ ישראל seeking practicing Jews. Death came to those who were caught learning תורה and fulfilling מצוות.

reading.p: אנטיכוס made special harsh decrees against three מצוות:
list: Jews were forbidden to keep שבת,
They were not allowed to follow the Jewish calendar - including ראש חודש and the Jewish ימים טובים,
Boys were forbidden to have a ברית מילה.

reading: These three מצוות show our constant אמונה in ה':

head: שבת
Calendar / ראש חודש
ברית מילה
rows:
Through resting on שבת, we show our אמונה that ה' created the world.
By keeping שבת holy, we demonstrate that ה' still creates and runs the world.
Through ראש חודש we turn regular days into ימים טובים, which shows that “time” itself which is a “symbol” of nature can and is - made holy.

Through the ברית מילה we show that the physical body is - and needs to be - holy.
Holiness is not only in thoughts, ideas, words and discussions, but our bodies are holy, and we must act and be holy.

reading: As time went on, the situation was getting worse. Many ספרי תורה were burnt – along with the teachers who taught from them. King אנטיכוס commanded his generals to have the מתיונים publicly demonstrate that they had left their people and were enjoying it. The מתיונים were increasing and influencing others to join them.
The Jewish Nation was in trouble.

The יוונים were very “advanced” people. They learned a lot and appreciated philosophy and logic. Their problem was that for them, everything had to “make sense.” They could not accept that there is something higher than our understanding.
They didn't tell us not to learn תורה or do מצוות. They could not accept our אמונה in ה', that we believe in an invisible, infinite G-d, Who created the world and continues to run it.

They could not accept that we do things even though we don't understand them, like the מצוות which have no explanation - the חוקים. All the rules of טמא and טהור, שעטנז, כשר etc. are מצוות that ה' gave us – without giving any reason for them. We do them only because ה' said to, there IS no other reason. This is what the יוונים could not handle.

They didn't mind us learning תורה. As long we read or study it as just a nice interesting “book”. They also saw the תורה as a very wise book that teaches us wonderful things and makes us smart – that part was fine. What they didn't like is that we keep the תורה holy, and learn it because it comes from ה', and ה' told us to learn it!

We see this idea in the תפילה of ועל הנסים which we say during חנוכה. As it describes the חנוכה story, it says that the יוונים tried “להשכיחם תורתיך ולהעבירם מחוקי רצונך” - to make them forget your תורה, and to remove them from the statutes (laws) of Your will.
These words of the תפילה were written carefully and accurately. It does not say that they tried to make us forget “The תורה” – rather, it says – “Your תורה” – Hashem's holy תורה.

reading.h: The inner Jewish spark cannot be ruined

reading: Each person is like a whole world. Many of the things that happen in the world also happen right inside us.

The fact that they found a jug of pure, untouched oil, teaches us that there is a place within ourselves that always remains holy and pure. Nothing can ruin or defile it. In our נשמה there are 5 levels. נפש, רוח, נשמה, חיה and יחידה. The level of יחידה – which means “unity” or “alone” is the level of our נשמה that is an actual part of ה'. It is always holy and nothing we can do can negatively affect it.

It is from this level of the נשמה that we have the ability and desire for מסירת נפש – to sacrifice our lives rather than turn away from ה'. Throughout our history people died “על קידוש ה'” – to sanctify the Name of ה'. These holy people were not always holy in their daily life activities. Many of those who died did not live a life of an observant Jew. However, when the choice came to officially turn away from ה', to ח"ו bow to an idol or similar – it was this פינטעלע איד the innermost holy spark of ה' that is within us – the יחידה of the נשמה, which burst into a big flame in these people. When the יחידה of the נשמה is reached, a person knows and feels that s/he is a part of ה' and will not – and truly cannot - separate him/herself from ה'.

name: מהדרין / מן המהדרין
focus: The three levels, why everyone lights the best way, and doing mitzvos beautifully.
today: Which mitzvah can you do in a more beautiful way?
overview: There is a basic way to do a mitzvah, and then there is the most beautiful way - mehadrin min hamehadrin. Chanukah teaches us to always do mitzvos in the best way we can.

reading.h: Two ways to do a מצוה

reading.p: Generally, there are 2 ways מצוות are performed:
list: בהידור or מהדרין. The “beautiful” way, meaning, doing more than the הלכה requires, beyond the letter of the law.

reading: Usually, most people do מצוות, like מזוזה, תפילין, סוכה, אתרוג, כשר, שבת etc. the “regular way,” and some perform it beyond the letter of the law - the more beautiful, the מהדרין way.
On חנוכה, everyone lights the מנורה on a third, higher level: מהדרין מן המהדרין – The most beautiful of the beautiful!

bullets: The basic מצוה of חנוכה is to light just one candle each night, in each house.
מהדרין is to have one candle for each person in the house.
מהדרין מן המהדרין is for each person to light an additional candle, each night – meaning, each person lights their own מנורה – and that is the way we do it.

reading: So we see that on חנוכה, everybody does the מצוה in the best of the best way!

reading.p: In doing the מצוה the best possible way, each person lights their own מנורה.
The מנורה should (best) be made of a metal. If you can afford it, a silver מנורה is best.

reading.h: Why do we all light this way?

reading: Why do we all light the מנורה the מהדרין מן המהדרין way?

When our ancestors searched for pure oil, although they were able to use the impure oil - they didn't. They searched and searched – until they found one pure jug of oil. They acted לפנים משורת הדין - beyond the letter of the law. ה' responded with the miracle of the שמן, which was “לפנים משורת הדין” of nature.
Every חנוכה, we connect to the same high level. Our נשמה feels that high level, and inspires us – every one of us – unconsciously - to do the מצוה in the best possible way, מהדרין מן המהדרין.

The חנוכה lights that shone then – and now – also come from the holy light that ה' hid at the beginning of Creation. This light is hidden in the תורה, and is available to צדיקים today, and will also shine for us all when משיח comes.
Families light the מנורה in different ways. All of them follow בית הלל and add one more light each night.

bullets: Many Ashkenazi families: each person lights their own מנורה. This is the custom the booklet describes above.
Many Sephardi families: one מנורה for the whole household, usually lit by the head of the family. That way anyone looking can tell which night of חנוכה it is.
In many families, including Chabad families, girls and women do not light their own מנורה. They are included in the lighting of the head of the household.

reading: How does your family light? Ask at home, then compare with your partner's family.

As you may have realized, the Jewish people decided unanimously that they want to do this mitzvah in the most beautiful of the beautiful way. It doesn't matter that they don't all necessarily do every other mitzvah in the best way possible. The light of Chanukah gets special treatment. Because the light of Chanukah is lit in the dark of winter when darkness is strongest.

name: תפילות
about: Hallel, Al HaNissim, Haneiros Halalu, Maoz Tzur.
focus: What each tefillah means, who wrote it, and when we say it.
today: How can you say thank you to Hashem today?
overview: On Chanukah we add special tefillos of thanks, like Al Hanissim and Hallel, and we say brachos when we light the menorah. These tefillos retell the whole Chanukah story.
reading: The story of חנוכה is summed up very well in the תפילה of praise and thanks we say daily during חנוכה – “על הנסים”:

reading.title: על הנסים
reading.en:
[We thank You ה']
For the Miracles, the Redemption, the Mighty Acts, the Saving Acts and for the Wars (Wonders) that You have done for our fathers, in those days at this time.
[Thank You!]
In the days of מַתִּתְיָהוּ the son of יוֹחָנָן the כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל (from the) חַשְׁמוֹנָאִי (family) and his sons.
When the wicked Syrian-Greek-Hellenistic government rose up against Your People יִשְׂרָאֵל,
to make them forget Your תּוֹרָה
and to move them away from the decrees of your will.
But you, in your great mercies
stood by them in the time of their distress.
You waged their battles,
defended their rights
and avenged the wrong done to them,
You delivered;
the mighty into the hands of the weak,
the many into the hands of the few,
the impure into the hands of the pure,
the wicked into the hands of the righteous,
the sinners into the hands of those who occupy themselves with Your תּוֹרָה.
You made a great and holy Name for Yourself in Your world, and brought about the great deliverance and the redemption for your People יִשְׂרָאֵל, to this very day.
Then Your children entered the holy place of your house, cleansed your הֵיכָל, purified your בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, kindled the lights of your holy courtyards and instituted these eight days of חֲנוּכָּה, to give thanks and praise to your great Name.

reading.title: Blessing #1 – before lighting the Menorah
reading.en: Blessed are You Hashem our G-d, King of the Universe, Who made us holy with His commandments and commanded us to kindle the light(s) of Chanukah

reading.title: Blessing #2 – before lighting the Menorah
reading.en: Blessed are You Hashem our G-d, King of the Universe, Who made miracles for our fathers, in those days, at this time.

reading.title: Blessing #3 – Say only the first time you light this year.
reading.en: Blessed are You Hashem our G-d, King of the Universe, Who kept us alive, sustained us, and allowed us to reach this occasion.

reading.p: Before lighting the מנורה, we make three ברכות on the first night, and two ברכות on the rest of the nights. The three ברכות are:

reading: On the rest of the nights we skip the ברכה of שהחיינו.

reading.p: After the ברכות are said, light the first candle. Say הנרות הללו as you light the rest.

reading.title: הנרות הללו
reading.en: We kindle these lights on account of the miracles, the deliverances and the wonders which thou didst work for our fathers, by means of thy holy priests. During all the eight days of Chanukah these lights are sacred, neither is it permitted us to make any profane use of them; but we are only to look at them, in order that we may give thanks unto thy name for thy miracles, thy deliverances and thy wonders.

prayer:
מָעוֹז צוּר יְשׁוּעָתִי
לְךָ נָאֶה לְשַׁבֵּחַ
Mighty Rock of my salvation, It is a delight to praise You

תִּכּוֹן בֵּית תְּפִלָּתִי
וְשָׁם תּוֹדָה נְזַבֵּחַ
Restore my House of Prayer, and we will offer there a thanksgiving offering.

לְעֵת תָּכִין מַטְבֵּחַ
מִצָּר הַמְנַבֵּחַ
אָז אֶגְמוֹר
בְּשִׁיר מִזְמוֹר
חֲנֻכַּת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
When you will “rid us of our enemies,” then I will finish with a song of praise (for) the Dedication of the Altar.

reading.h: Al Hanissim in davening and bentching

reading.p: All eight days of חנוכה we say “על הנסים” in the שמונה עשרה.
If you forgot to say “על הנסים”:
bullets: if you remembered before you said ה''s name of the next ברכה, say it right then.
If you remembered after you said ה''s name, - continue Davening.

reading.p: We also say the “על הנסים” during ברכת המזון – Bentching. If you did not say it in its proper place, and already said ה''s name of the next ברכה, then, when you reach the “הרחמן's” you say a special “הרחמן” and continue with “בימי מתתיהו” etc.

reading: We complete the הלל all eight days of חנוכה.

reading.p: During חנוכה, we do not say תחנון.

The תורה is read every day of חנוכה. Each day, we read about the קרבנות הנשיאים – the presents the leaders of the שבטים brought at the original חנוכת המשכן, when they completed building the משכן in the desert.

reading: On all eight days of Chanukah, full Hallel is recited after Shacharit morning prayers. Additionally, the Al haNissim blessing is inserted into the Amidah prayers and the Grace after Meals.

In the synagogue, the portion of the nesi'im (Bamidbar 7), which recounts the offerings brought by the nasi [prince] of each of the twelve tribes when the Mishkan, the Tabernacle, was dedicated, is read from the Torah.

name: Maccabees in modern times
about: Jews in our times who kept the light going.
focus: Jews in our times who kept Torah and mitzvos when it was hard, and how we can do the same.
today: Who are the Maccabees of our time, and how can you be one?
overview: The Maccabees fought with courage thousands of years ago, but their job is not finished. Every Jew who adds light to the world today is a modern-day Maccabee.
reading: How can little me… illuminate the world – you ask? Am I the President…? I'm just a kid! I don't even have a good flashlight!!

Ahhh… the trick is that when a lot of little “regular” people create light in their own personal space – when each person brightens up his/her environment – all the lights then join together and connect into one big flame… and the world is a perfect place – once again.

Before there were lights in the streets, there were street lamps. The lamps had oil and wicks, like candles. Each evening, as it would begin to get dark, the lamplighter would go from lamp to lamp, lighting each one with the flame at the end of his long torch. The lamps would shed a sweet light, far and wide.

The people of the world are like those old fashioned street lamps. We are the lamplighters. Our job is to go around lighting the lamps, with the light of תורה and מצוות - creating light wherever we are. At home, in school, on the playground, in the park, on the bus – anywhere and everywhere – we bring joy, warmth and holy light to the people and the place.
One of the beautiful things about our lamplighter job, is that once we light a lamp – it remains lit. We do not need to stand there and keep the fire going.

People like light. They enjoy the light we bring them. It brightens up their life and warms them. Soon, they are ready to share some of their own light with others. They spread the light you shared with them, and some other light they found on their own – because of you. The lamp you lit goes on and lights up other lamps. The person you inspired and helped, inspires and helps others. The people whom s/he inspires, goes on to brighten up others. Soon the whole world is bright and beautiful. This is the world of משיח.
The חנוכה message is that we can illuminate our world, one lamp at a time, one person at a time, one place at a time, starting with ourselves and our homes.

reading.p: מתתיהו's message: “מי לה' אלי” spread like wildfire and his small band grew day by day.

reading: The Jewish warriors waged guerrilla warfare against the mighty armies of אנטיכוס IV. When the King's armies would march toward the hills - the Jews would ambush them from caves, behind trees, and it seemed like from everywhere. The Syrian-Greek armies were terrified to fight the Jews and were beaten every time.

יהודה gathered his men together and reminded them that it is not the military power or sophisticated weapons that win a war – it is ה''s help! “Few can win against many and the weak can win against the strong, as we've seen so many times before – if only ה' wants! ה' will surely fight for us in this final battle.”

Today, ברוך ה' we do not have the same challenges as our ancestors did years ago. We do not need to die, to live Jewish. We can live like Jews wherever we wish. This however, has become our challenge today – to actually live like a Jew, amongst the rest of the world who looks and thinks differently from us. Our challenge is to remain pure and holy in this world where it is so easy to get lost in the false, fleeting pleasures of the secular ideas, fashions and trends. In some ways, our challenge to live like a Jew is a greater one than to die as a Jew.

We need to dig deep into ourselves and reach the deeper levels of our נשמה where the truth is clear and obvious, and allow our נשמה to shine away our own darkness. Then we can fulfill our mission, to brighten up our surroundings with the light of our נשמה – the light of ה'.

name: Light vs. darkness
about: A little light pushes away a lot of darkness.
focus: The message of the lights. (The Miracle, Oil, and Number 8 groups cover the story.)
today: How can you bring light to someone this week?
overview: A little bit of light pushes away a lot of darkness. Chanukah teaches us to fight the darkness in the world by adding more and more light.

reading.h: The חנוכה message: light over darkness

reading: Imagine walking into a completely dark room? So dark you can almost feel the darkness. There may be things in the room – there may not – there may be others in the room – there may not. You don't know because you cannot see, it's too dark. And maybe a little scary.
Then, you light a candle. Ahhh. The light of just one candle illuminates the whole room. Suddenly, you are not afraid - you are able to see. (Hey, there really aren't any monsters!)

Our lives are full of battles. Most of them are within ourselves. We are in constant combat with the “enemy” inside us. The enemy is also known as the “יצר הרע”. The internal enemy tries to convince us not to do what we should. Sometimes it tries to convince us to do something wrong.

bullets: The יצר הרע is compared to darkness.
ה', our נשמה and the יצר טוב - are compared to Light

reading: In regular warfare, it's only natural that the bigger and stronger army wins. The more soldiers you have, the stronger your army is – the better your chances of winning.

In צבאות ה' – ה''s army, the rules are different. ה' is compared to Light. A little light chases away a lot of darkness. When we are fighting for ה', whether in a battle with other nations, or right within ourselves – the regular rules of nature do not apply.
In our battlefield, inside or out, Right wins against Might. Few win against Many, and Weak wins against Strong.
חנוכה is our reminder that we (the good guys) will always win. For, in the end, Light will always win over darkness.
Following ה''s path, we are certain to succeed. The Greatest Warrior is on our side.
Light is powerful. It brightens up our life.
Good is often compared to light. When someone makes you feel good you say s/he “brightened up my day”. When a pleasant person enters a room, s/he “brightens up the room.”
Goodness, kindness, happiness and similar - are compared to light.
Light brings actual life to plants.
One of the most wonderful things about light is that:

reading.banner: A Little Light Dispels a Lot of Darkness.

reading: תורה and מצוות are the purest and brightest lights. One little מצוה can brighten up your life. One little מצוה you do can brighten up another's life. A little תורה can brighten up your whole attitude, forever.
חנוכה is all about Light (– not so much about the fight.) ה' created this world and put us here with a mission:

head: The מנורה
Our lesson
rows: We light the מנורה at nightfall
To brighten up the darkness of the night - the places that are spiritually “dark” and people whose lives are not yet “brightened” by the תורה and מצוות.

reading: The חנוכה lights that shone then – and now – also come from the holy light that ה' hid at the beginning of Creation. This light is hidden in the תורה, and is available to צדיקים today, and will also shine for us all when משיח comes.

According to the accepted Jewish custom, we begin the first night of Chanukah by lighting just one candle, and each night we add another, until all eight are lit on the final night. Because though a little light might push away much darkness, the world often shows us that a little light isn't enough. So we shine more. And we shine more. And we don't stop until the night itself has been entirely lit up.
